install.isolation: installed with pip --target into /tmp/flyvis-libs, OUTSIDE the repository and outside the Flymon venv; never committed
install.note: an initial torch/torchvision ABI mismatch (torchvision resolved from PyPI against a CPU torch) was fixed by reinstalling torchvision from the same CPU index

why_not_run: flyvis direction selectivity is a property of TRAINED networks (Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024).

The package ships no bundled pretrained ensemble and exposes no download helper or CLI entry point in this install; the pretrained checkpoints are hosted externally and were not obtainable in this environment.

An untrained, connectome-initialised flyvis Network would not be expected to show direction selectivity, so running it would not constitute a positive control and could be mistaken for evidence against the stimuli.
Per the Experiment-17 brief, dependency work was bounded rather than escalated.

substitute_positive_control.method: Hassenstein-Reichardt elementary motion detector applied directly to the same Experiment-5 retina samples of the unchanged Experiment-16 stimuli
substitute_positive_control.rationale: Answers the same question flyvis was meant to answer (are the stimuli and retinal sampling capable of yielding direction selectivity?) with no external dependency and full transparency.
substitute_positive_control.outcome: Maximal direction selectivity (|DSI| = 1.0, sign flips with direction); gray and frozen controls give exactly 0; temporal shuffle suppresses 76%; time reversal flips the sign.

conclusion: Stimulus adequacy is SUPPORTED by the substitute positive control; hypothesis H3 (inadequate stimuli) is rejected without needing flyvis.
